quotes.speaker: Nick Nurse
quotes.summary_phrase: Nick Nurse on the challenges of integrating new lineups
quotes.excerpt: I think it's some good, some bad. Good to get them out there for the first time.
quotes.quote: I think it's some good, some bad. I think good to get them out there for the first time. Obviously, it's what preseason is for. I think there was some really good things happening right off the bat, a bunch of back cuts and good passing, but then I think there was segments where, obviously, we turned the ball over a lot, which you can never do, but just a little clunky in segments too. But again, it's preseason, first time they're together. I think you look at it as what's good and what are the learning experiences, things that we can improve on, and then try to get them together, keep them together, and get them together as much as we can in the next time we get that chance in practice.
quotes.social_post: Nick Nurse says the Sixers were a little clunky in their preseason debut but noted some good ball movement and back cuts. He emphasized that the team is still working on connectivity as they integrate new lineups.

quotes.speaker: Nick Nurse
quotes.summary_phrase: Nick Nurse on Joel Embiid's performance and conditioning
quotes.excerpt: I thought he ran the floor pretty well. He just needs to get some rust off.
quotes.quote: I thought he was very good. Joel got like 23, 22, 23 minutes there, almost 24. That was good to see. I think again, getting him out there, I thought he ran the floor pretty well. I think that he just needs to get some rust off and get out there and get playing, which was which was great to see. I mean, obviously, he'd play a lot better than that. He'd be the first one to say that, but I also was I'm extremely happy that he was out there with the group and I thought he was playing very hard, which was which was great to see.
quotes.social_post: Nick Nurse was happy to see Joel Embiid back on the floor for 24 minutes. He noted that while Embiid has some rust to shake off, he was pleased with the star center's effort and conditioning.

quotes.speaker: Nick Nurse
quotes.summary_phrase: Nick Nurse on the team's defensive intensity and physicality
quotes.excerpt: They're going to come at you a lot deep, a lot of guys really flying around.
quotes.quote: It is good. I kind of mentioned it in pregame, they're going to come at you a lot deep, a lot of guys really flying around on offense, picking up on defense, and I think that is good for us. It's good to see that now and get the feel of it, but yeah, I think we'll see some of that throughout the year, so it's good to see it now.
quotes.social_post: Nick Nurse says facing a high intensity opponent in the preseason is good for the Sixers to get a feel for the defensive pressure they will see throughout the year.

quotes.speaker: Nick Nurse
quotes.summary_phrase: Nick Nurse on LeBron James' role as an offensive creator
quotes.excerpt: He's a great, great passer and I was certainly on display tonight.
quotes.quote: He's a great, great passer and I was certainly on display tonight. I thought he did a number of getting the ball up the floor, do a couple long ones for layups, he threw some middle ones for layups, and then he threw some in the quarter court for guys cutting, and again, just I thought movement, ball movement around the perimeter and stuff like that is good. He thought he really read the game well.
quotes.social_post: Nick Nurse praised the playmaking of LeBron James tonight, noting that he read the game well and did a great job of finding teammates for layups in both transition and the half court.

quotes.speaker: Nick Nurse
quotes.summary_phrase: Nick Nurse on managing player minutes during the preseason
quotes.excerpt: In these situations, you just don't go quite as long as normal quite yet.
quotes.quote: I think that certainly discuss it, and it was going to be first half minutes, right? That's the first thing. And then, I think in these situations, you just don't go quite as long as normal quite yet, right? So a nine-minute stint is seven, what would be a normal one, or six and a half or something, and then maybe you would have held him out earlier, but since you took him out earlier, you can put him back and run him through the quarter and stuff. You're just trying to get to that number, 16-18 minutes, doesn't really matter how you do it right now, but a little bit shorter stints than you would normally see probably.
quotes.social_post: Nick Nurse explains his approach to preseason minutes, noting that he is using shorter stints to get players to their target numbers while they adjust to game speed.

quotes.speaker: Nick Nurse
quotes.summary_phrase: Nick Nurse on addressing turnovers and team connectivity
quotes.excerpt: That's just a little bit of a connectivity time issue.
quotes.quote: They did a good job of turning us over. I think that's part of what I talked about at the beginning. I think we find the open man and then the next pass out, and again, that just that's just a little bit of a connectivity time issue, I think. I think we got great size and great passing there, so that should smooth itself out.
quotes.social_post: Nick Nurse attributes the team's high turnover count to a lack of connectivity early on, but remains confident that their size and passing ability will smooth things out as they play more together.

quotes.speaker: Nick Nurse
quotes.summary_phrase: Nick Nurse on defensive performance and schematic experimentation
quotes.excerpt: There's a couple things schematically we were doing that probably wouldn't do.
quotes.quote: I felt pretty good early on. I know they scored a bunch right out of the shoot, but almost every one of them were fairly long, fairly long possessions, fairly contested, a couple bounced around the rim and went in. I was thinking like we're not like smothering them, but we're doing a really nice job of keeping them in front. There's a couple things schematically we were doing that probably wouldn't do, and cost us a couple baskets here and there that we wouldn't normally do, but it's kind of the stage we're at with our scheme, so we just decided to go with some of those things. Again, it's the same at that end, too, the communication, the connectivity will just just just improve, but I think it was a decent place to start against a team who was really firing around, really fired up.
quotes.social_post: Nick Nurse says the Sixers experimented with some defensive schemes tonight that they would not normally run, acknowledging that it cost them a few baskets but provided a good baseline for improvement.
